task_message:
Case M42: segment the myxoid soft-tissue tumor on this T2-weighted MRI.

Volume: 261x261x321 voxels, 1 mm isotropic. Budgets: max 40 tool calls / 15 model prompts / 10 min wall time.
Start with `seg_open`. Finish with `seg_finish`.
final_assistant_text:
I finished case M42.

**What I did:**
1. **Orientation** — Opened the case (T2, 261×261×321, 1 mm). Contact sheets in axial, coronal and sagittal showed a single lower limb spanning ankle (low axial indices) to knee (high indices), with fat-suppressed-like muscle signal and many small bright vessels.
2. **Lesion search** — Scanned the whole volume at multiple levels. The scattered small bright dots and chains (subcutaneous/soleal veins, skin markers) were rejected as normal anatomy; the only space-occupying, lobulated, markedly T2-hyperintense structure was in the deep posterior compartment around axial slices 155–195.
3. **Segmentation** — Seeded with a positive point on the lesion core, then added points on its contiguous lobules (growing to 4.5 mL), and ran `seg_refine` to clean the boundary (final 4.2 mL, single component).
4. **Verification** — The final review showed the green outline following the hyperintense mass in all three planes, with no lesion tissue in the "just past the end" slices; the automatic candidates (C1–C5) were thin elongated structures within fat planes = vessels, so they were not accepted.

**Result:** one connected lesion, 4.2 mL, extent axial 155–194, coronal 110–131, sagittal 135–158; confidence **medium** (boundary is clean in all planes, but the lesion is small/elongated so partial-volume at the ends leaves some uncertainty).
